regions.name: Central Amazon
regions.why: The largest rain forest: are its dry seasons getting hotter and drier?

T2M.label: Air temperature
T2M.simple: How warm the air is 2 metres above the ground — what a thermometer in the shade shows.

TS.label: Surface temperature
TS.simple: The temperature of the surface itself — soil, rock, sea water or ice — which can be much hotter or colder than the air above it.

PRECTOTCORR.label: Precipitation
PRECTOTCORR.simple: How much rain and snow falls, in millimetres of water per day (1 mm on one square metre is one litre). MERRA-2 corrects its model rain with rain gauges and satellite observations.

GWETROOT.label: Root-zone soil wetness
GWETROOT.simple: How wet the soil is where plant roots drink (roughly the top metre): 0 % is bone dry, 100 % is completely soaked.

EVLAND.label: Evaporation from land
EVLAND.simple: Water rising from the land into the air — from wet soil, lakes and plant leaves (transpiration) — in millimetres per day.

RH2M.label: Relative humidity
RH2M.simple: How close the air is to being saturated with water vapour: at 100 % it cannot hold more and dew or fog forms.

TQV.label: Water vapour in the air column
TQV.simple: All the water vapour above a spot, from the ground to the top of the atmosphere — the millimetres of water you would get if it all rained out at once.

SLP.label: Sea-level pressure
SLP.simple: The weight of the air above a spot, as if measured at sea level (about 1013 hPa on average): low pressure brings storms, high pressure fair weather.

WS10M.label: Wind speed
WS10M.simple: How fast the wind blows 10 metres above the ground (10 m/s is 36 km/h).

TROPT.label: Tropopause temperature
TROPT.simple: The temperature at the tropopause, the ceiling of the weather layer of the atmosphere: about 8 km up near the poles and 17 km up in the tropics.

links.text: Air temperature and Surface temperature leave their norm in the same months, the same way: 138 times, where chance at the same moment of the record would give 70 (p = 4e-35; z = 14.1 against the same reading with one of them moved 1 to 5 years, beyond the shared trend and the persistence of each). So often, both ways (98 % and 95 %), that Eva takes them for one dynamic seen through the identity: in 10 months one left its norm without the other.
links.model_note: the 2-metre air temperature of a reanalysis is computed from the surface temperature and the lowest model level: this link is partly the model's own arithmetic

links.text: Surface temperature and Relative humidity leave their norm in the same months, in opposite directions: 102 times, where chance at the same moment of the record would give 61 (p = 7e-12; z = 9.9 against the same reading with one of them moved 1 to 5 years, beyond the shared trend and the persistence of each). So often, both ways (70 % and 69 %), that Eva takes them for one dynamic seen through a mirror: in 88 months one left its norm without the other.
links.model_note: both series come from the MERRA-2 reanalysis, not from two independent instruments: confirm it with an independent dataset before calling it a finding

story.text: Air temperature — Central Amazon: +0.37 °C per decade (95 % range +0.287 to +0.451). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 5.2e-13, t-test p = 3e-05. Eva: Since 2011, 77 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Surface temperature — Central Amazon: +0.38 °C per decade (95 % range +0.292 to +0.459). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 2.8e-12, t-test p = 3.9e-05. Eva: Since 2011, 78 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Precipitation — Central Amazon: -0.50 mm/day per decade (95 % range -0.646 to -0.329). Significant falling trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 3.8e-07, t-test p = 4.7e-05. Eva: Since 2011, 81 % of months came out lower than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Root-zone soil wetness — Central Amazon: -2.4 % per decade (95 % range -3.08 to -1.57). Significant falling trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 3.2e-07, t-test p = 0.0014. Eva: Since 2011, 78 % of months came out lower than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Evaporation from land — Central Amazon: -0.18 mm/day per decade (95 % range -0.266 to -0.102). Significant falling trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level.
